title: Testing and Quality Gates: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of the test pyramid, unit vs integration vs end-to-end tests, linting and static analysis, code coverage, flaky tests and CI quality gates.

chapters.title: Test Pyramid Mental Model
points: Test pyramid: many fast unit tests at the base, fewer integration tests in the middle, a few slow end-to-end (E2E) tests at the top
Going up the pyramid means slower runs, higher cost and flakiness, broader coverage and harder debugging
Fast feedback rule: push each check to the lowest level that can still catch the bug
Ice-cream cone anti-pattern: mostly manual or E2E tests with few unit tests gives slow, brittle suites
Testing trophy variant: emphasizes integration tests, with static analysis as the base, when units are thin glue code

chapters.title: Unit vs Integration vs End-to-End
points: Unit test: one function or class in isolation, with dependencies replaced by mocks, stubs or fakes; runs in milliseconds with no network or disk
Integration test: several real components together, such as the service plus a real database or API contract; catches wiring, schema and config bugs
E2E test: drives the whole system through the UI or public API like a user, for example Playwright or Cypress on a login-to-checkout flow
Comparison row: unit = fast and precise failures; integration = medium speed and realistic; E2E = slow, most realistic, fewest in number
Mistake: over-mocking so tests pass while production breaks; assert behaviour and outputs, not internal calls

chapters.title: Linting and Static Analysis
points: Linter: checks style and likely bugs without running the code (ESLint, Ruff, Pylint, golangci-lint); formatters such as Prettier or Black only fix layout
Static analysis: type checkers (tsc, mypy) and security scanners (Semgrep, CodeQL, Bandit) find defects, taint flows and unsafe patterns before runtime
Everyday commands: eslint . --fix, ruff check ., mypy src/, tsc --noEmit
Run lint and type checks in a pre-commit hook and again in CI so skipped local hooks cannot bypass them
Mistake: blanket-disabling rules or adding ignore comments; fix the cause or suppress one line with a written reason

chapters.title: Code Coverage
points: Coverage measures the share of code executed by tests: line, branch (every if/else path) and function coverage
Branch coverage is stricter than line coverage: one test can hit a line while skipping the other branch of its condition
Everyday commands: pytest --cov=src --cov-branch, jest --coverage, go test -cover; reports come out as lcov or HTML
100% coverage does not prove correctness: executed code is not asserted code; use mutation testing (Stryker, mutmut) to check test strength
Mistake: chasing a coverage number with assertion-free tests; use the report to find untested paths and enforce a floor on new code

chapters.title: Flaky Tests and Quality Gates
points: Flaky test: passes and fails on the same code; usual causes are timing and sleeps, shared state or test order, unseeded randomness, real network or clock
Fix flakiness by waiting on conditions instead of sleeping, isolating state per test, injecting fixed clocks and seeds, and mocking external services
Quarantine a flaky test immediately by tagging it and tracking a ticket; auto-retry hides the problem and erodes trust in the suite
Quality gate: automated pass/fail checks in CI that block merge, such as tests green, lint clean, type check, coverage on new code at or above a threshold, no critical vulnerabilities
Mistake: gates that are slow or noisy get bypassed; run fast checks first, require them on protected branches, and gate new code rather than the whole legacy base

chapters.title: Testing and Quality Cheat Sheet
points: Pyramid ratio: roughly 70% unit, 20% integration, 10% E2E; place each check at the lowest level that catches the bug
Levels: unit = isolated and fast; integration = real components together; E2E = full user flow, few and critical only
Static checks: eslint . --fix, ruff check ., mypy src/, tsc --noEmit; run in pre-commit and CI
Coverage: pytest --cov=src --cov-branch, jest --coverage; prefer branch coverage, gate new code, verify strength with mutation testing
Flaky and gates: no sleeps, isolate state, seed randomness, quarantine rather than retry; a merge is blocked unless tests, lint, types and coverage all pass
